title: Coskeleta of truncated simplicial objects as finite limits, and their preservation
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits] and let $m\geq0$. Let $\Delta$ be the category of the ordered sets $[k]=\{0<\dots<k\}$ and order-preserving maps [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. For $n\geq0$ let $(\Delta/[n])_{\leq m}$ be the finite category whose objects are the morphisms $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$ of $\Delta$ with $k\leq m$ and whose morphisms $(\alpha':[k']\to[n])\to(\alpha:[k]\to[n])$ are the morphisms $\psi:[k']\to[k]$ of $\Delta$ with $\alpha\circ\psi=\alpha'$. For an $m$-truncated simplicial object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton] let $U(n):(\Delta/[n])_{\leq m}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$ be the functor $(\alpha:[k]\to[n])\mapsto U_k$, $\psi\mapsto U(\psi)$. Then: (1) the $m$-coskeleton $\operatorname{cosk}_mU$ of $U$ exists in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton]; one may take $(\operatorname{cosk}_mU)_n=\lim U(n)$, with $\operatorname{cosk}_mU(\varphi)$ for $\varphi:[n]\to[n']$ the morphism of limits induced by $\alpha\mapsto\varphi\circ\alpha$, and the counit $\varepsilon:\mathrm{sk}_m\operatorname{cosk}_mU\to U$ is an isomorphism; (2) if $\mathcal D$ is a category and $\Phi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is a functor preserving finite limits, then the simplicial object $\Phi\circ\operatorname{cosk}_mU$ of $\mathcal D$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] together with $\Phi(\varepsilon)$ is an $m$-coskeleton of the $m$-truncated simplicial object $\Phi\circ U$; consequently, if $K$ is a simplicial object of $\mathcal C$ whose canonical morphism $K\to\operatorname{cosk}_m\mathrm{sk}_mK$ is an isomorphism, then $\operatorname{cosk}_m\mathrm{sk}_m(\Phi\circ K)$ exists and the canonical morphism $\Phi\circ K\to\operatorname{cosk}_m\mathrm{sk}_m(\Phi\circ K)$ is an isomorphism; (3) for a morphism $\beta:U\to U'$ of $m$-truncated simplicial objects of $\mathcal C$ there is a unique morphism $\operatorname{cosk}_m\beta:\operatorname{cosk}_mU\to\operatorname{cosk}_mU'$ with $\varepsilon'\circ\mathrm{sk}_m(\operatorname{cosk}_m\beta)=\beta\circ\varepsilon$; this is functorial, so $\operatorname{cosk}_m\beta$ is an isomorphism when $\beta$ is, and when $\Phi$ is as in (2), $\Phi\circ\operatorname{cosk}_m\beta=\operatorname{cosk}_m(\Phi\circ\beta)$ for the coskeleta of (2); (4) in particular, for a category $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal C=\mathrm{PSh}(\mathcal E)$ the category of presheaves of sets on $\mathcal E$ (which has finite limits, computed objectwise), every evaluation functor $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F(V)$, $V$ an object of $\mathcal E$, preserves finite limits, so (2) and (3) apply to it, with $\mathcal D$ the category of sets.

proof.text: The objects of the truncated simplex category inject into Fin (m + 1) by their lengths. Its opposite is finite as well. Simplex morphisms are finite by Mathlib, and opposites and the fully faithful inclusion inherit finite hom sets. Objects of StructuredArrow n (inclusion m).op are the image of the finite dependent sum of truncated objects x and arrows n -> inclusion.op.obj x; its hom sets inject into the corresponding truncated hom sets by taking the right component. Thus every indexing category is a FinCategory.

Finite limits give HasPointwiseRightKanExtension for every truncated object U. Take R = inclusion.op.ran and epsilon = inclusion.op.ranCounit. Mathlib isPointwiseRightKanExtensionRanCounit proves the pointwise limit description, and ranCounit has the right Kan extension property. Full faithfulness of the inclusion and IsPointwiseRightKanExtension.isIso_hom show that every epsilon.app U is an isomorphism.

Apply hom_ext_of_isRightKanExtension to the two maps b and R.map beta. The assumed counit equation and naturality of ranCounit identify their composites with the counit, proving uniqueness of the induced map. Functoriality is built into Mathlib ran.

A finite-limit-preserving functor Phi preserves each limit of a StructuredArrow diagram because that category is finite. Mathlib preservesPointwiseRightKanExtensionAtOfPreservesLimit and preservesPointwiseRKEOfHasPointwiseAndPreservesPointwise therefore give preservation of the right Kan extension. Removing the identity components of the associator gives the image counit exactly as stated. Apply hom_ext_of_isRightKanExtension in the image category; the required counit equation for the whiskered map follows by applying Phi.map to each component of naturality of ranCounit.

For the final clause compare c prime with whiskerRight c Phi using hom_ext_of_isRightKanExtension. Their composites with the image counit are identities: this is assumed for c prime, and for the whiskered c follows by applying Phi.map to the original counit equation componentwise. Hence c prime equals whiskerRight c Phi. The latter is an isomorphism since c is. The presheaf evaluation case is a specialization of this general theorem and requires no separate presheaf-limit lemma in its proof.

lean.statement: theorem truncatedCoskeletonFiniteLimits (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [HasFiniteLimits C] (m : ℕ) : ∃ (R : SimplicialObject.Truncated C m ⥤ SimplicialObject C) (ε : R ⋙ SimplicialObject.truncation m ⟶ 𝟭 _), (∀ U, (R.obj U).IsRightKanExtension (ε.app U)) ∧ (∀ U, Nonempty ((Functor.RightExtension.mk (R.obj U) (ε.app U)).IsPointwiseRightKanExtension)) ∧ (∀ U, IsIso (ε.app U)) ∧ (∀ (U U' : SimplicialObject.Truncated C m) (β : U ⟶ U') (b : R.obj U ⟶ R.obj U'), (SimplicialObject.truncation m).map b ≫ ε.app U' = ε.app U ≫ β → b = R.map β) ∧ ∀ (D : Type w) [Category.{v'} D] (Φ : C ⥤ D), PreservesFiniteLimits Φ → (∀ U, (R.obj U ⋙ Φ).IsRightKanExtension (Functor.whiskerRight (ε.app U) Φ)) ∧ (∀ (U U' : SimplicialObject.Truncated C m) (β : U ⟶ U') (b : R.obj U ⋙ Φ ⟶ R.obj U' ⋙ Φ), (SimplicialObject.truncation m).map b ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (ε.app U') Φ = Functor.whiskerRight (ε.app U) Φ ≫ Functor.whiskerRight β Φ → b = Functor.whiskerRight (R.map β) Φ) ∧ (∀ (K : SimplicialObject C) (c : K ⟶ R.obj ((SimplicialObject.truncation m).obj K)), (SimplicialObject.truncation m).map c ≫ ε.app ((SimplicialObject.truncation m).obj K) = 𝟙 _ → IsIso c → ∀ c' : K ⋙ Φ ⟶ R.obj ((SimplicialObject.truncation m).obj K) ⋙ Φ, (SimplicialObject.truncation m).map c' ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (ε.app ((SimplicialObject.truncation m).obj K)) Φ = 𝟙 _ → IsIso c')
